chunks: And by this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, brother of Muglis al-Sayfari, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to fast so much that it was said he never broke his fast, and he used to break his fast so much that it was said he never fasted. Then he fasted the fast of Dawud (peace be upon him), fasting one day and breaking one day. Then he passed away while fasting the three days of the month. He said: 'These equal the fast of a lifetime and remove the heat of the chest.'
I said: 'May I be your ransom, which days are they?' He said: 'The first Thursday of the month, the first Wednesday after the tenth of it, and the last Thursday of it.'

I said: 'And why did these days become so?' He said: 'Because the communities before us, when punishment was sent down upon them, it was sent down on these days. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) fasted all of these days because they are the days of fear.'

key_terms.الْأَيَّامُ الْمَخُوفَةُ: The days of fear, referring to days when divine punishment was historically sent down
key_terms.صَوْمُ دَاوُدَ: The fast of Dawud (David), referring to fasting one day and breaking one day alternately
key_terms.وَحَرُ الصَّدْرِ: The heat of the chest, referring to spiritual anxiety or restlessness
key_terms.يَعْدِلْنَ الدَّهْرَ: They equal the fast of a lifetime/age

ai.seo_question: Which specific days of the lunar month did the Prophet Muhammad fast to emulate Dawud and avoid divine punishment?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) adopted the fasting of Dawud (peace be upon him)—alternating days—culminating in the specific triad of the first Thursday, the Wednesday after the tenth, and the last Thursday of the month. These days are identified as 'the fearful days' (al-ayyam al-makhufah), as divine punishment historically descended upon previous nations during this period, making the Prophet's fast a protective expiation for a lifetime's sins and a lifetime's sins and a remedy for spiritual anxiety (wahar al-sadr).
